text:
Aliaksei Protas scored 25 goals for Washington last season, a big step for a 6'6" third-round pick who had needed time to find his NHL game. Eighteen games into this one, he has 2 goals and 10 points, and none of those points have come on the power play. He is on a four-game point streak, with one goal and four assists.

The goals are the part that looks like bad luck. His expected goals, the quality of his chances, are 3.71, and he is scoring on 7.7% of his shots, below the bottom of the range our numbers expect for him. His chance rate has dipped from last season too, so it isn't only finishing. At five-on-five, though, the Capitals have had about 55% of the chance quality with him on the ice, better than without him.

Evolving-Hockey's read on him last season was a forward who drives offense (92nd percentile among forwards) at a defensive cost (bottom 10% at preventing chances). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that 61% of his exits leave the zone with the puck. With 16 minutes a night and a heavy shot, the goals are the piece we'd watch.
headline: Aliaksei Protas is setting up goals, not scoring them
